name: Masala Idli
steps: Let the cooked idlis cool until firm, then cut them into bite-sized cubes. Chop onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger and coriander separately.
Heat oil in a wide pan, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then cook onion, ginger and chilli for 4–5 minutes until the onion softens.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Cook uncovered for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until the tomato becomes a thick coating rather than a watery sauce.
Add the idli cubes and toss gently for 2–3 minutes to coat all sides without breaking them. Cover for one minute so the centres heat through.
Scatter coriander over the hot idli and serve at once. Using cooled idlis helps each cube hold its shape in the masala.
tips: This is a useful fresh preparation for cooled idlis, but the cubes must be heated fully before serving.
passiveTime: No passive preparation required when cooked idlis are ready.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
